comments.content: The name `workflow_is_running_cmd` deviates from the project's naming convention for Tauri commands. Adjacent workflow commands (`workflow_run`, `workflow_stop`, `workflow_decompose`, `workflow_save`, `workflow_load`, etc.) and the vast majority of commands in this `invoke_handler` block do not use the `_cmd` suffix. Consider renaming to `workflow_is_running` (or `workflow_run_status`) to match the established convention; the frontend can still invoke it via the renamed string.

The `should_emit` doc comment (lines 67–75) lists three variants (Manual / Scheduled / Batch) but the match arm now also handles `Workflow`. Add a Workflow bullet to the doc so the public contract stays in sync with the implementation and future readers don't miss the fourth unattended-execution case.

Layout regression: the wrapping div with mt-1 always renders, so the bottom margin is now applied even when both progress is null and data.saved is true (i.e., a saved workflow with no execution in progress). In the original code, mt-1 lived on the conditionally rendered p tag, so the margin only appeared when the unsaved hint was shown.

comments.content: `TaskExecOrigin::Workflow` is the only newly added variant in this match arm, but `tests` covers only `Manual` and `Scheduled` paths of `should_emit`. A future refactor that drops Workflow from this arm (or changes its column gating) would slip through CI. Mirror `should_emit_scheduled_ignores_status` with `TaskExecOrigin::Workflow` (assert `Some` for `todo`/`doing`/`done`/`None` columns) so the unattended-execution contract is regression-protected alongside the existing Scheduled case.

Nested ternary in the `title` attribute violates the project rule "Nested ternary expressions are not allowed", and three-branch logic in a tooltip is harder to maintain than a lookup. Extract a small helper or a const map.

comments.content: `stopRun` is not guarded against re-entrancy and does not flip `running` to `false` after the invoke resolves, so the Stop button stays clickable (and the title still reads "停止…") until the next 5 s poll reconciles state. During that window rapid clicks fire `workflow_stop` repeatedly. Add a local "stopping" pending guard and/or optimistically clear `running` (the backend is meant to be idempotent, but the button should still settle immediately for the operator).

`running` is not reset when the user switches workflows (`openWorkflow`) or starts a new blank canvas (`createBlank`). Side effects: (1) the Stop button keeps rendering against an `activeId` that no longer refers to the running workflow, and `stopRun()` then issues `workflow_stop` on the wrong workflow id; (2) in `createBlank` the button stays visible with no `activeId` to act on. Either reset `running` (and rely on the next poll to re-set it for the new workflow) or — better — key `running` to `activeId` so it cannot leak across selections.

`workflow_is_running_cmd` is fired after `workflow_load` completes without an `openSeqRef` race guard, so if the user switches workflows mid-flight, an older workflow's `is_running` response can overwrite the newer one (the `else` clauses on `workflow_load` are guarded, but the chained `is_running_cmd` is not). Capture the `seq` (or stash `activeId` at call time) and only call `setRunning` if the open sequence still matches.

Race condition: `setRunning(true)` is set optimistically before `await invoke("workflow_run", ...)` resolves. The polling effect starts as soon as `running` becomes `true`, but the backend only registers the runner inside `workflow_run` (after the registry-lock release and DAG build). If the invoke takes longer than the 5 s poll interval, `workflow_is_running_cmd` can return `false` while the original `workflow_run` is still pending, causing `setRunning(false)` to overwrite the optimistic `true`. The UI then flips back to "开始执行" and the user can click again — producing a duplicate `workflow_run` (backend's RUNS registry will reject it, but only after a wasteful round-trip and UI flicker). Gate the polling's state write until the in-flight invoke settles, e.g. via an `invokeInFlightRef` checked inside the `.then` before calling `setRunning(v)`, or skip starting the interval until after `await invoke` resolves.

Polling swallows backend errors silently via `.catch(() => {})`. If `workflow_is_running_cmd` fails persistently (network down, command panic, registry poison), the interval keeps firing forever and the user sees a permanently "执行中" button that can never reset because the polling chain keeps erroring out. At minimum log the error (`console.warn`) so it surfaces in dev tools; ideally surface a single transient failure notice so the user knows the displayed state may be stale.

`activeId` is now in the `rfNodes` deps but only feeds the `progress` ternary, which short-circuits to `null` when `running` is `false`. Switching the workflow while not running (`createBlank` → another `openWorkflow`) still rebuilds the entire `rfNodes` array (and re-renders every TaskNode) even though the output is byte-identical. Splitting the goal node's data into its own `useMemo` keyed on `[name, goal, savedSnapshot, running, activeId, tasks]` would keep `rfNodes` independent of the rarely-changing progress fields, and lets the existing `nodes.map` memo drop `running`/`activeId` from its deps.
